description: Canonical experiment catalog for the Adaptive eBPF Security Lab. This is the single source of truth for experiment definitions. Per-tool *.json files in this directory are the original per-run definitions and are preserved for provenance; the pipeline reads this catalog.

falco.label: Falco
falco.configured_events: execve/execveat via custom container process-execution rule + built-in ruleset

tracee.label: Tracee
tracee.role: eBPF telemetry collector (no signatures engine configured in this lab)

tetragon.label: Tetragon
tetragon.role: eBPF tracing-policy telemetry (no alerting/enforcement configured in this lab)

experiments.title: Sensitive File Access
experiments.purpose: Determine whether reading a sensitive file (/etc/shadow) inside a container is visible to, and detected by, each runtime-security system.
experiments.expected_observation: The open of /etc/shadow is visible at the kernel level; Falco's built-in sensitive-file rule is expected to raise a security detection.

experiments.title: Process Execution
experiments.purpose: Establish baseline process-execution observability for benign commands inside a container.
experiments.expected_observation: execve events for sh, id, and uname are visible with container context.

experiments.title: Network Activity
experiments.purpose: Determine whether an outbound HTTPS request from a container is observable, distinguishing process-execution telemetry from network-connection visibility.
experiments.expected_observation: Process-execution telemetry for wget is expected. Network-connection (connect) visibility depends on whether each tool is configured with a network event source.

experiments.title: Indirect Execution
experiments.purpose: Test whether introducing an additional shell layer (execution indirection) reduces process-execution observability relative to the E02 baseline.
experiments.expected_observation: All execution stages (both shell layers and the final command) remain visible.

experiments.title: Timing Variation
experiments.purpose: Test whether inserting controlled two-second delays between commands reduces process-execution observability relative to the E02 baseline.
experiments.command: sh -c 'echo TIMING_TEST_1; sleep 2; echo TIMING_TEST_2; sleep 2; id'
experiments.expected_observation: All execution events remain visible despite the inserted delays.
experiments.shell_payload: echo TIMING_TEST_1; sleep 2; echo TIMING_TEST_2; sleep 2; id

experiments.title: Repeated Baseline Consistency
experiments.purpose: Run a deterministic benign process-execution workload five times to describe repeatability of process-execution telemetry capture (exploratory, not statistical proof).
experiments.expected_observation: Each of the 5 trials captures the same sh,id execution chain; trial-to-trial variation (if any) is described, not aggregated into a significance claim.

experiments.title: Sensitive vs Benign File Access
experiments.purpose: Compare telemetry and rule coverage for reading a sensitive file (/etc/shadow) versus a harmless ordinary file, using only safe read operations.
experiments.expected_observation: Both reads generate openat telemetry; a sensitive-path rule (where configured) should distinguish the sensitive read. Tetragon tracing policy captures both pathnames but does not alert on either.

experiments.title: Network Observability & Policy Coverage
experiments.purpose: Evaluate network observability versus network-specific detection, after inspecting each tool's actual network event/policy configuration. Separates telemetry from alerts; labels detection NOT EVALUATED where no network policy exists.
experiments.expected_observation: Process-execution telemetry is captured by all tools. Socket/connect visibility depends on configuration: Tracee has a connect event source; Falco and Tetragon (this lab) have no network policy, so their network detection is NOT EVALUATED, not failed.

experiments.title: Process Sequence & Timing Comparison
experiments.purpose: Derived comparison of the baseline (E02), indirect-shell (E04) and timing-variation (E05) process chains and captured event ordering, using existing evidence. No new capture.
experiments.expected_observation: The process chain changes across variants (sh,id → sh,sh,id → sh,sleep,sleep,id) while every stage remains observable. This describes observability, not evasion.
